scope: Source and test change only: registry regime evaluator module, two tables, four routes, registry dependency lock, compose read-only governed mount. No deployment, no hosted run, no model fitted on Taiwan history.

decisions_recorded_before_coding.C1_governed_data_read: The registry reads governed rows itself, in process, through services.research.regime.features.load_governed_observations (every input passes feature_catalogue.read_feature_series, point in time), from the source-ingestion normalized store. docker-compose mounts the existing source-ingest-data volume read-only into the registry at /data/source-ingest (REGISTRY_REGIME_STORE_ROOT). The registry never writes that volume. Rejected: caller-supplied observations (the daily cycle would have to ship years of rows per call).
decisions_recorded_before_coding.K5_dependencies: Statistical dependencies run in the registry image, not a separate worker. Measured with venvs built from the lock files on python 3.12 (site-packages, du -sm): current registry lock 74 MB; registry lock plus numpy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.6, scipy 1.17.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, statsmodels 0.15.0 and their dependencies 485 MB; difference +411 MB (about 6.5x the site-packages). Reasons: one process boundary keeps idempotent evaluate, the lifecycle writes and the model reads in one place and testable without a queue; the registry image already COPYs the repo, so the vendored jumpmodels and the research features module are present. The separate-worker fallback stays open if the image size becomes a deployment problem. ruptures is not needed (audit use in research only).
decisions_recorded_before_coding.dependency_lock: dependencies/locks/services-registry.txt was edited by hand at the versions pinned in services-research.txt because uv is not available to the worker; the header says so. A venv installed with plain pip from that file imports services.registry.main and the evaluator, vendored jumpmodels included (checked).

Finding for the research task: services/research/regime/registration.py approves with a caller-supplied 'approver', which the registry rejects with 400 'Caller-supplied approver is retired; use a Governance decision reference' when the real approval path is used. Registration of candidates works; approval needs a Governance decision reference. Not changed here (outside this task's scope); the HTTP tests here use the existing Governance approval transport double (advance_registry_http) for the approval step.
Revised-input detection runs only when the caller passes verify_inputs=true; the default call never re-reads governed data (acceptance 3).
Models are selected market-wide (not tenant-filtered); strategy records are tenant-scoped by the strategy spec's owner tenant.
The Postgres commit serialises concurrent evaluators with an advisory transaction lock; the individual puts are not one transaction.
All numeric thresholds (5-session transition window, 0.5 mixed, 0.3 low confidence, family defaults, 20-session short holding horizon) are design proposals to be calibrated.
